To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a robot can learn to coordinate speech and gestures by using reinforcement learning, (2) a robot can improve its performance by learning to coordinate speech and actions based on the audio feedback it receives, (3) a robot can use a multimodal interface to improve its performance in a task, and (4) a robot can be trained to learn a multimodal interface that allows it to communicate with users in natural ways.

(1) a robot's ability to learn from speech can improve when speech and actions are integrated, (2) a robot's learning of speech can be improved when the robot's actions are coordinated with speech, (3) a robot's performance can be improved when it learns to coordinate actions and speech, (4) a robot's speech can be improved by learning from its actions, and (5) a robot's actions can be improved by coordinating them with its speech.

(1) the combination of multiple sources of information, such as audio, visual, and motion data, can improve performance in interactive systems; (2) the use of machine learning techniques can be applied to improve the robustness of interactive systems; and (3) the use of a machine learning technique, namely, deep learning, can improve the accuracy of a system that is based on multiple sources of information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how machine learning methods can be applied in the context of multiple modalities of human-machine interaction.
how to best learn from and with multimodal interaction data.
how to learn to use and combine different modalities to improve the performance of interactive systems and robots.

machine learning for multiple modalities in interactive systems and robots is a growing research area that will be increasingly important in the near future.
this special issue provides a snapshot of the current state-of-the-art of the application of machine learning to multiple modalities in interactive systems and robots.
the research articles in this special issues demonstrate that machine learning is a valuable and necessary ingredient of multiple modality interactive systems and robots.

we have shown how machine learning can help interactive systems and robots to learn from and adapt to users, and to coordinate multiple modalities.
we have developed machine learning methods for multiple modalities of interactive systems and robots.
we have been able to successfully apply machine learning techniques to the problem of multimodal interaction, which has led to improved performance of the interactive systems that we have developed.

machine learning is a powerful tool that can be used to improve the performance of interactive systems.
machine learning methods for interactive systems and robots that use multiple modalities can be very useful in improving their performance.
machine learning can provide a powerful framework for developing systems that are able to interact with humans through more than one channel.
